segments.text: If you're addicted to coffee, I actually have good news. A recent study showed that those who drank two to three cups of coffee per day were associated with an 18% lower risk of dementia. That's great, but uh I drink tea.

Well, people who drank one to two cups of tea per day also showed a similar association with cognitive health. However, in this particular study, decaf drinkers showed no significant association. This suggests that caffeine may be the key driver of these neuroprotective effects. [music] But, here's the catch. Caffeine has a 5-6 hour half-life. So, a cup of coffee at 3:00 p.m. leaves half a cup of coffee in your system at 9:00 p.m. That lingering caffeine wrecks your sleep. And poor sleep has tons of negative effects on cognitive [music] health. Despite the benefits of caffeine, I choose to not have it. For me, it creates a

physiological roller coaster. After 3 days, I'm addicted. If you're going to have multiple cups of coffee or tea, try to consume them earlier in the day. While caffeine may support the brain, interfering with sleep hurts it.
